⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A funny smell when an oven is first turned on can be normal if it's a new appliance or hasn't been used for a while, as manufacturing oils burn off. Is the smell sharp and acrid (like burning plastic/wire) or just dusty/foody? 2. If it is electrical-smelling, stop using the oven immediately and isolate the power at the fuse box until a qualified engineer can inspect the mains connection behind the appliance. If it's just dusty, run the oven empty at 180°C for 30 minutes to clear any residues.
